title: Tools and Equipment Accommodations
description: Physical tools, assistive technology, and learning aids the student can use during instruction. Use when the student needs alternative input/output methods, organizational supports, sensory tools, or adaptive materials to access curriculum.

source.name: ADayInOurShoes — Ultimate List of IEP Accommodations, Modifications & Strategies (SDIs)

accommodations.text: Visual cues in locker, lunch box, and on desk.
Written schedules on locker and lunch box.
Special seating such as seat pads or sit-upon balls.
Adaptive equipment: pens, pencils, calculators, fidget toys, large-print books, audio materials, etc.
Use of FM headsets to either block out noise with music or transmit the teacher's voice; use Beats or other socially acceptable headphones to block outside noise.
Use of a scribe or oral testing for open-ended or essay formats.
Extra set of textbooks — one set for home, one for school.
Provide notes, outlines, or organizers with key concepts or terms highlighted.
Remind student to wear glasses or hearing aids.
Allow use of preferred writing implement.
